disposition_reason: Per-crop mean concentrations are only in Figure 1; the text prints the cross-crop ranges for arsenic, nickel, aluminium and copper with the crops at the extremes, which are extracted. Risk tables give soya bean arsenic as not detected.

study.design: market survey; 144 purchases composited into 24 samples (4 markets x 6 crops)
study.market: Nasarawa main market (A, B), Mararaba Udege (C) and Laminga (D) markets, Nasarawa LGA, Nigeria
study.method: aqua regia and H2O2 wet digestion; ICP-OES (Agilent 720), US EPA 200.7 adapted
study.qa: spike recoveries 93-117%; reference material mentioned but not named

findings.material_label: Food crops (black eye bean, soya bean, millet, sorghum, sesame, locust bean)
findings.group: range across six crop means, four markets
findings.notes: Lower end of the range of crop mean arsenic concentrations; text says arsenic occurred 'primarily in black eye bean and sesame'. Table 1 lists soya bean arsenic as ND.

Upper end of the crop-mean range; text states sesame consistently records the highest arsenic. Arsenic at 5-31 mg/kg by ICP-OES is far above typical crop values; the authors note it greatly exceeds earlier Nigerian data.

unresolved: Per-crop and per-market means (with SD) for As, Ni, Al, Cu are figure-only (Figure 1) and were not read.
Magnesium, potassium, calcium and sodium ranges (e.g. Mg 4,152-13,956 mg/kg) printed in text were not extracted as they are macro nutrients.
Hazard quotients and cancer risks (Tables 1-3) were not back-calculated into concentrations.
Locust bean is missing from Tables 1 and 2 but present in Table 3.
